attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “This is the uniform version of Friedgut’s theorem [5, Theorem 1.1 in the February 3, 1998 author manuscript].” Its bibliography: “[5] Ehud Friedgut. Boolean functions with low average sensitivity depend on few coordinates. Combinatorica, 18(1):27–35, 1998. https://doi.org/10.1007/PL00009809.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 2.2 (Friedgut’s junta theorem) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of directed feedback vertex set” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-directed-feedback-vertex-set-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 606657a956af61c2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every b ≥ 0 and α > 0, there is a finite integer Junif(b, α) with the following property. For every finite S and every Boolean function f : 2S → {0, 1} with I1/2(f) ≤ b, there is a Boolean function e f, depending on at most Junif(b, α) coordinates, for which Pr R∼µS 1/2 [ f(R) ̸= e f(R) ] ≤ α. The bound is independent of |S|.
